ai.title: Fix .env.worktree precedence in bun wrapper
ai.summary: The .bin/bun wrapper now loads .env.worktree after Infisical cache to ensure worktree overrides take precedence. Added finalize_and_exec and load_worktree_env functions to standardize secret loading across all execution paths. Updated knowledge.md to document the correct precedence order and project-root lookup behavior. This fixes issues where cached Infisical values would incorrectly override worktree-specific configurations like ports.

eli5.text: Developers working on this project can now rely on their local worktree settings (like custom port numbers) to override the shared secret values without needing to manually reset them each time, so if you look you'd see the project correctly honoring per-worktree configurations instead of falling back to cached defaults. The system now loads worktree-specific files last to lock them as the final word, keeping things consistent regardless of where you run the command from.

ai.title: CLI logout returns success for invalid tokens
ai.summary: The `/api/auth/cli/logout` endpoint now returns `{ success: true }` instead of a 401 `INVALID_AUTH_TOKEN_MESSAGE` when no active session is found. This change treats logout attempts with already invalid or expired tokens as a successful no-op to prevent confusing error messages in the npm app. The update is scoped to `web/src/app/api/auth/cli/logout/route.ts`.

eli5.text: If you use the CLI tool to log out and your login session was already expired or missing, the logout command will no longer show a confusing error message saying your credentials are invalid. Instead, it simply reports success because being already logged out is treated the same as successfully logging out now. You will notice this the next time you run the logout command after your session has expired - no error screen, just a clean confirmation.
